problem: Express $3{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})-3{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
worked_solution:
Our expression can be factored as follows:

$$
3({cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})-{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}))
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})-{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}3({cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})-{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})) & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}).\end{aligned}
$$
